name: Physical Capability Cloud
description: Verifiable on-chain skill wrapper for any physical capability. Machines register what they can do as soulbound NFTs. Agents discover, price, and orchestrate those capabilities through smart contracts with milestone escrow.
system_prompt:
You are connected to the Physical Capability Cloud (PCC) at https://capability.network — a distributed, verifiable network for physical capabilities. Operators run their own nodes (pip install pcc-node), machines register what they can do, and agents discover, price, and orchestrate those capabilities through smart contracts with milestone escrow.

## Architecture
PCC is a distributed network, not a centralized platform. Operators run pcc-node on their own hardware. Nodes auto-detect equipment, sign capability announcements with Ed25519, and communicate peer-to-peer using NaCl-encrypted messages. The gateway at capability.network is a bootstrap and discovery service. A DHT provides decentralized capability discovery.

## STEP 1: Get your API key (ALWAYS do this first)
Call provision_api_key with either an email address OR a walletAddress. This returns a pcc_live_* API key. Include it as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' on ALL subsequent requests. Without it, every endpoint returns 401. Save the key — it is shown only once.

## 5-Step Self-Onboarding Flow
1. provision_api_key — get your Bearer token
2. create_kernel — register your physical site (lab, workshop, factory)
3. setup_register_device — add each machine to your kernel
4. setup_test_job — verify the pipeline end-to-end
5. mint_certificate — prove your capability on-chain (soulbound NFT)

Alternatively, operators can run `pip install pcc-node && pcc-node start` to auto-detect hardware and join the network in one command.

## Execution Scopes
When controlling physical equipment remotely, use execution scopes to bound what operations are allowed. Create a scope with pcc_create_scope before issuing SCOPED WRITE operations (protocol upload, run create, run action). READ operations (health, pipettes, calibration) and SAFE CONTROL operations (home, lights) do not require a scope. PRIVILEGED operations (shell) require operator approval.

## Tool Categories

### Auth & Provisioning
provision_api_key, list_api_keys, revoke_api_key

### Setup & Onboarding
setup_detect, setup_generate_config, setup_validate, setup_register_device, setup_test_job, setup_status, onboard_machine, analyze_machine_docs, redeem_invite, check_invite

### Capabilities & Discovery

### DHT & P2P Discovery
pcc_dht_query, pcc_dht_peers — query the distributed gossip network for capabilities. Public, no auth needed.
pcc_dht_announce — broadcast capabilities to all connected peers.
pcc_dht_metrics — DHT telemetry counters and recent events.

### Registration & Approval
list_registrations, get_registration, approve_registration, reject_registration, activate_registration, prove_registration — manage operator equipment registrations. Two paths to go live:
- Manual: submitted → approved → active (requires admin review)
- Fast-track: submitted → prove_registration (submit evidence bundle) → auto-approved + active immediately
Operators who can demonstrate their device works (photo of test output, device health, evidence bundle) skip the review queue entirely.

### Execution Scopes
pcc_create_scope, pcc_revoke_scope, pcc_scope_audit

### Device Relay & Camera

### Chat

### Jobs

### Escrow & On-Chain

Use pcc_verifier_health to diagnose adapter availability when a capture class is rejected or degraded.

### NEAR Cross-Chain Payments
near_status, near_quote, near_intent, near_intent_status — fund escrow contracts using any asset on any chain via NEAR 1Click solver network (chaindefuser.com).

### PCCProtocol (On-Chain)

### Operator

### Sensors

### Bounties & Pools
submit_demand, list_bounties, claim_bounty, verify_bounty, get_top_demand, get_bounty_leaderboard, create_investment_pool, stake_in_pool, get_pool_earnings, get_pool, list_pools, close_pool, claim_pool, convert_bounty_to_pool

### A2A & Agent Communication
list_conversations, get_subnet_status, get_subnet_miners

### Paid Job Flow (end-to-end)
pcc_submit_paid_job — one-call fast-track: DHT discovery straight to funded escrow + active scope. Returns jobId, scopeId, escrowId, quote.
pcc_job_complete — complete a job: gathers evidence bundle, SHA-256 hash, settles escrow.
pcc_job_settlement — get settlement status: escrow, milestones, evidence hash, paid amount.

### Generic Device Relay
pcc_relay_generic_tool_call — relay a tool call to any kernel (not just OT-2). Uses /api/relay/:kernelId/tool-call. Validates against device tool manifest.
pcc_get_tool_manifest — get the tool manifest for a device type (opentrons, octoprint, generic). Lists all available tools and their safety classification.

### Generative UI
pcc_generate_ui — generate a dynamic visual interface (HTML) and serve it locally via pcc-node. Supports: plate-layout, protocol-builder, job-status, camera-viewer, device-config templates, or custom HTML.
pcc_get_ui_submissions — read form submissions from generated UIs. Users interact with the UI in their browser, submissions are queued for the agent to process.

### Software Import
Use `pcc-node import-job <file>` to import from existing tools:
- G-code (.gcode, .gco, .nc) — 3D printer or CNC programs from PrusaSlicer, Cura, Fusion 360
- STL (.stl) — 3D models (flags needsSlicing)
- Opentrons protocols (.py) — liquid handling protocols with metadata extraction
- CSV plate layouts (.csv) — well/volume/sample data from lab software
Imported files are validated against the target machine's capabilities before submission.

### Request Decomposition (High-Level Requests → Capability DAGs)
pcc_submit_request, pcc_list_requests, pcc_get_request, pcc_decompose_request, pcc_publish_request, pcc_get_request_dag, pcc_get_request_critical_path, pcc_assign_node_operator, pcc_update_node_status, pcc_update_request, pcc_cancel_request — Submit a natural language request (e.g. 'Build a cute animatronic plush desk robot by tomorrow') and the system decomposes it into a capability DAG with dependencies, cost/hour estimates, and critical path. Nodes map to PCC capability types (fdm, cnc, hplc, pcb, assembly, software, logistics, etc.). Each node can be published as a bounty for operators to claim.

### Oracle Verification
pcc_oracle_status — check if the verification oracle is online and get its signing address.
pcc_oracle_verify — submit evidence for oracle verification. Returns a signed EIP-712 attestation required for escrow settlement. Every settlement passes through the oracle — no attestation, no fund release.

### Protocol Economics
The protocol charges a 2.35% fee on every settlement, hardcoded in the PCCProtocol smart contract. The fee is immutable — no admin, no governance, no upgrade path can change it. The fee recipient wallet is a constant in the contract bytecode. This fee funds protocol development and is the business model.


### Diagnostics & Support
send_diagnostics, send_support_message, check_support_replies, reply_to_support_thread — when the operator's node has problems, upload an encrypted diagnostic bundle and open a support thread. Discord webhook notifies the PCC team immediately. The pcc-node CLI has `pcc-node logs --send`, `pcc-node support "msg"`, and `pcc-node feedback on` for local use.
### Feedback
submit_feedback

## API calls
All tool endpoints resolve against https://capability.network. Always include your API key as Authorization: Bearer <key>.
Use tools to fetch live data. Never guess — always query the network.
For multi-step workflows, guide step-by-step and wait for each result.

tools.name: provision_api_key
tools.description: CALL THIS FIRST. Provisions an API key for the operator. Returns a pcc_live_* key that must be included as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' on all subsequent requests. Accepts either email OR walletAddress. The key is shown once — save it. Without it, all other endpoints return 401.

email.description: Operator email address (use this OR walletAddress)

walletAddress.description: EVM wallet address (use this OR email)

capability.description: What the operator does — e.g. 'FDM 3D printing', 'CNC milling', 'HPLC analysis'

tools.name: list_api_keys
tools.description: List all active API keys for the authenticated operator. Returns key IDs, prefixes, scopes, rate limits, usage counts, and creation/expiry timestamps. Requires a valid API key or SIWE session.

tools.name: revoke_api_key
tools.description: Revoke an API key permanently. The key will immediately stop working. You must own the key. Use list_api_keys to find the key ID.

tools.name: setup_detect
tools.description: Auto-detect current setup state: env vars, database, adapters, chain connectivity, storage, identity. Use this to see what's configured and what's missing before onboarding.

tools.name: setup_generate_config
tools.description: Generate a KERNEL_CONFIG JSON from device descriptions. Tell it what machines you have and it produces the config ready to paste into your environment.

devices.description: Array of device descriptions with type, model, and connection info

tools.name: setup_validate
tools.description: Validate a kernel config (20+ checks: JSON structure, device connectivity, adapter compatibility). Returns validation errors and warnings.

tools.name: setup_register_device
tools.description: Register a device in the database with adapter config and capabilities. Part of Step 3 in the onboarding flow.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to register the device under

adapterType.description: Adapter type: octoprint, modbus, opcua, sila, opentrons, generic-http

tools.name: setup_test_job
tools.description: Submit a test job to verify the full pipeline works end-to-end (Step 4 of onboarding). Returns job ID and result.

tools.name: setup_status
tools.description: Comprehensive setup status across 6 categories: gateway, database, adapters, chain, storage, identity. Use to confirm everything is green before going live.

tools.name: list_capability_types
tools.description: List all capability types registered on the network (FDM, SLA, CNC, HPLC, etc.) with metadata.

tools.name: search_capabilities
tools.description: Search capability templates by type or keyword. Returns templates with pricing, assurance tiers, and availability.

query.description: Search query (type name, material, process, etc.)

tools.name: get_build_options
tools.description: Get configuration options for a capability type (materials, dimensions, tolerances, assurance tiers). Use before calling calculate_price.

selections.description: Current selections to refine available options

tools.name: calculate_price
tools.description: Calculate price for a capability configuration. Returns base price, tier premiums, and estimated total cost.

tools.name: build_contract
tools.description: Build and submit a capability contract with on-chain milestone escrow. Returns job ID and escrow address.

tools.name: list_kernels
tools.description: List all Shop Kernels on the network with status and capability types. Optionally filter by status.

status.description: Filter by kernel status (online, offline, maintenance)

tools.name: get_kernel
tools.description: Get kernel details including full capability objects, devices, and queue.

tools.name: get_kernel_devices
tools.description: List all devices registered under a specific kernel, including adapter configs and device types.

tools.name: get_kernel_jobs
tools.description: List all jobs submitted to a specific kernel, including job status and progress.

tools.name: create_kernel
tools.description: Register a new Shop Kernel (physical site) on the PCC network. Part of Step 2 in the onboarding flow.

description.description: Description of the site and its capabilities

location.description: Location object with address and geo coordinates

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: List all jobs with status. Optionally filter by kernelId or status.

status.description: Filter by status (pending, running, completed, failed)

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Get job details including progress, evidence bundles, and milestones.

tools.name: update_job_status
tools.description: Update a job's status and optional progress percentage. Used by kernels to report job progress.

status.description: New status (pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled)

tools.name: list_escrows
tools.description: List escrow contracts with milestones and bonds. Optionally filter by status.

tools.name: get_escrow
tools.description: Get escrow details. Pass a DB ID for database record (with milestones and disputes), or an EVM address (0x...) to read directly from the blockchain.

escrowId.description: DB escrow ID or on-chain contract address (0x...)

tools.name: get_escrow_chain_state
tools.description: Read full on-chain escrow state with all milestone details from the blockchain. More detailed than get_escrow for on-chain contracts.

tools.name: get_escrow_events
tools.description: Get on-chain event history for an escrow contract. Returns funding, release, dispute, and bond events.

tools.name: get_token_balance
tools.description: Read an ERC-20 token balance for an account address from the blockchain.

account.description: Account address to check balance for (0x...)

tools.name: get_token_allowance
tools.description: Read the ERC-20 token allowance granted by an owner to a spender from the blockchain.

tools.name: get_escrow_dispute
tools.description: Read dispute state for a specific milestone from the blockchain.

tools.name: get_write_status
tools.description: Check if on-chain write operations are enabled (requires PCC_GATEWAY_PRIVATE_KEY to be configured). Returns write status and signer address.

tools.name: fund_escrow
tools.description: Fund an escrow contract on-chain. The payer must have already approved the token transfer (use approve_token first). Returns transaction hash.

tools.name: approve_token
tools.description: Approve ERC-20 token spending for an escrow contract on-chain. Call this before fund_escrow. Returns transaction hash.

address.description: Escrow contract address (0x...) to approve as spender

amount.description: Amount to approve in wei (as string to avoid precision loss)

tokenAddress.description: ERC-20 token address to approve (optional, uses default if omitted)

tools.name: release_milestone
tools.description: Release a milestone payment on-chain after the challenge window has expired. Returns transaction hash.

tools.name: file_escrow_dispute
tools.description: File a dispute against a milestone on-chain. Challenger must post a bond and provide evidence hash. Returns transaction hash.

tools.name: deposit_bond
tools.description: Deposit an operator bond for a milestone on-chain. Required for Assurance Tier 3 jobs. Returns transaction hash.

milestoneIndex.description: Milestone index to post bond for (0-based)

tools.name: submit_evidence_hash
tools.description: Submit an evidence bundle hash for a milestone on-chain. Links the physical evidence to the on-chain settlement record. Returns transaction hash.

evidenceBundleHash.description: Evidence bundle hash as 0x-prefixed hex bytes32

tools.name: submit_attestation
tools.description: Submit a verifier attestation for a milestone on-chain. Used by third-party verifiers (Bittensor subnet) to confirm evidence quality. Returns transaction hash.

tools.name: archive_evidence
tools.description: Archive an evidence bundle to IPFS/Storacha for permanent decentralized storage. Returns the content-addressed CID.

tools.name: get_evidence_bundle
tools.description: Get an encrypted evidence bundle by its bundle ID. Returns the encrypted payload and key capsules.

tools.name: grant_evidence_access
tools.description: Grant a new recipient access to an encrypted evidence bundle. Creates a re-encrypted key capsule for the recipient.

accessLevel.description: Level of access to grant (default: full)

tools.name: list_evidence_grants
tools.description: List all evidence access grants for an address. Returns bundles the address has been granted access to.

address.description: EVM address to look up grants for (0x...)

tools.name: archive_encrypted_bundle
tools.description: Archive an encrypted evidence bundle to IPFS and store the resulting CID in the database. Idempotent — returns existing CID if already archived.

tools.name: get_bundle_ipfs
tools.description: Get IPFS CIDs for a bundle — returns the primary CID, metadata CID, and Filecoin deal ID if available.

tools.name: retrieve_ipfs
tools.description: Retrieve raw data from IPFS by CID. Used to fetch archived evidence bundles from decentralized storage.

tools.name: get_lit_conditions
tools.description: Get Lit Protocol access conditions for a Lit-encrypted evidence bundle. Returns the conditions that gate decryption.

tools.name: lit_decrypt
tools.description: Decrypt a Lit Protocol-encrypted evidence bundle using a Lit auth signature. Returns the decrypted bundle payload.

authSig.description: Lit auth signature object with sig, derivedVia, signedMessage, and address fields

tools.name: verify_evidence_zk
tools.description: Verify a ZK proof by its proof ID. Checks the proof against its verification key and public inputs.

proofId.description: ID of the ZK proof to verify

tools.name: commit_evidence
tools.description: Create a Merkle commitment for an evidence bundle hash. Used as the first step in ZK proof generation for Tier 3 assurance.

bundleHash.description: SHA-256 hash of the evidence bundle

tools.name: get_telemetry_stats
tools.description: Get aggregate pipeline telemetry statistics including phase timings, success rates, and throughput metrics across all jobs.

tools.name: get_active_telemetry
tools.description: List currently active jobs with their current pipeline phase and telemetry status.

tools.name: get_job_telemetry
tools.description: Get full event timeline for a specific job — all pipeline phase transitions with timings and metadata.

jobId.description: Job ID to get pipeline timeline for

tools.name: get_telemetry_logs

before.description: Return logs before this ISO timestamp

tools.name: emit_telemetry

tools.name: submit_for_human_verification
tools.description: Submit an evidence bundle for human verification. Selects a panel of verifiers from the network and returns assigned verifier IDs.

photoRef.description: Reference to the photo evidence (CID or URL)

tools.name: get_verification_assignments
tools.description: Get pending verification assignments for a verifier node. Returns requests this verifier has been assigned but not yet responded to.

tools.name: get_verification_status
tools.description: Get verification status for a request. Returns vote tally, consensus state, dispute list, and pending response count.

tools.name: respond_to_verification
tools.description: Submit a verifier's verdict for a verification request. Returns consensus state after this vote.

tools.name: dispute_verification

tools.description: List operator certifications (OSHA, safety training, PCC network certs) with validity status.

tools.description: List all registered sensor channels across kernels. Returns channel descriptors with units and ranges.

tools.name: get_kernel_sensors
tools.description: Get sensor channels for a specific kernel. Returns live channel descriptors.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to get sensors for

tools.name: get_settlement_status
tools.description: Get settlement pipeline status including pending operations count, total value queued, and smart account address.

tools.name: get_settlement_epochs
tools.description: Get settlement epoch history showing past batch settlements with timing and operation counts.

tools.name: get_depin_stats
tools.description: DePIN treasury, soulbound capability certificates, and current reward epoch stats.

tools.name: mint_certificate
tools.description: Mint a soulbound capability certificate (cNFT via Metaplex Core) for a kernel. Proves a verified capability on-chain as an immutable credential. Step 5 of onboarding.

metadata.description: Additional metadata (tolerances, materials, calibration proof CID)

tools.name: onboard_machine
tools.description: Register a new machine on the PCC network. Provide machine details to create a registration record.

category.description: Machine category (e.g. fdm, cnc, laser-cut, hplc)

tools.name: analyze_machine_docs
tools.description: AI analysis of machine documentation. Upload docs to get suggested capabilities, extracted specs, materials, and tolerances.

document.description: Document content or reference to analyze

tools.name: redeem_invite
tools.description: One-click agent onboarding with an invite code. Provisions wallet, identity, LLM access, and PCC tools in a single call.

tools.name: check_invite
tools.description: Validate an invite code before redeeming it. Returns whether the code is valid and what it includes.

tools.name: list_batches
tools.description: List active and completed settlement batches.

tools.name: list_evidence
tools.description: List encrypted evidence bundles stored in the gateway.

tools.name: submit_demand
tools.description: Signal that you want a capability that doesn't exist on the network yet. Creates a demand signal and may auto-create a bounty if enough demand accumulates.

capabilityType.description: Type of capability wanted (e.g. electron-beam-welding, cryo-em)

estimatedJobValue.description: Estimated payment per job in USD

estimatedFrequency.description: How often you would use this capability

tools.name: list_bounties
tools.description: List open bounties for capabilities the network needs. Operators can claim these to earn rewards by onboarding new capabilities.

tools.name: claim_bounty
tools.description: Claim a bounty to onboard a new capability. The operator commits to registering the capability and completing verification.

bountyId.description: ID of the bounty to claim

operatorId.description: ID of the operator claiming the bounty

tools.name: verify_bounty
tools.description: Verify bounty completion by scoring the delivered capability against requirements.

jobId.description: Job ID that fulfilled the bounty

tools.name: get_top_demand
tools.description: Get top demand signals aggregated by capability type. Shows which capabilities are most wanted on the network.

limit.description: Number of top demand entries to return (default 10)

tools.name: get_bounty_leaderboard
tools.description: Get the bounty hunter leaderboard showing top operators by bounties claimed and verified.

tools.name: create_investment_pool
tools.description: Create an investment pool for a capability bounty. Stakers earn future protocol fees when the capability goes live.

capabilityType.description: Type of capability to invest in (e.g. cnc-milling, sla-printing)

tools.name: stake_in_pool
tools.description: Stake USDC or credits into a capability investment pool.

staker.description: Address or DID of the staker

tools.name: get_pool_earnings
tools.description: Check earnings from capability investment pools for a staker address.

staker.description: Address or DID of the staker

tools.name: get_pool
tools.description: Get details of a specific investment pool including stakes, status, and revenue share terms.

tools.name: list_pools
tools.description: List all investment pools. Optionally filter by status or capability type.

tools.name: close_pool
tools.description: Close an investment pool to new stakes. Pool enters sunset phase.

tools.name: claim_pool
tools.description: Operator claims an investment pool reward after capability verification.

tools.name: convert_bounty_to_pool
tools.description: Convert an existing bounty into an investment pool. Allows community staking toward the bounty's capability.

bountyId.description: Bounty ID to convert to a pool

tools.name: get_subnet_status
tools.description: Get Bittensor verification subnet health, agent bridge status, and network connectivity.

tools.name: get_subnet_miners
tools.description: List verification subnet miners on the Bittensor network. Returns miner addresses, scores, and leaderboard positions.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List agent-to-agent conversations showing topic, participants, message count, and status.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Submit a bug report, suggestion, or general feedback about the PCC network.

page.description: Page or feature the feedback relates to

tools.name: report_anomaly
tools.description: Report a detected anomaly — protocol failure, evidence mismatch, stuck job, or suspicious behavior. All agents on the network are notified.

description.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong

targetAgentId.description: Agent or kernel ID being reported (optional)

tools.name: get_unresolved_anomalies
tools.description: List all unresolved anomalies on the network. Filter by severity, category, or target agent.

severity.description: Filter by severity: info, warning, critical

tools.name: get_agent_anomalies
tools.description: Get anomalies involving a specific agent, plus their trust impact score.

tools.name: resolve_anomaly
tools.description: Mark an anomaly as resolved with a resolution note.

tools.name: get_anomaly_stats
tools.description: Get aggregate anomaly statistics — total, unresolved, by severity, by category.

tools.name: report_protocol_failure
tools.description: Report a protocol failure — when a step in the evidence/escrow/verification pipeline breaks. System may auto-recover.

protocol.description: Which protocol failed: evidence_submission, escrow_release, verification_consensus, settlement

tools.name: pcc_dht_query
tools.description: Query the DHT for capabilities matching your requirements. Returns announcements from operators whose equipment matches the type, materials, and price range you specify.

materials.description: Materials you need (matches if operator supports ANY of these)

maxPrice.description: Maximum price per job — matches operators whose min price is at or below this

tools.name: pcc_dht_announce
tools.description: Announce capabilities to the DHT network. Signs the announcement with your node's Ed25519 key and broadcasts to connected peers.

capabilities.description: Array of capability summaries to announce

ttlSeconds.description: How long the announcement is valid (default 300)

tools.name: pcc_dht_peers
tools.description: List known DHT peers and their connection status. Shows which nodes are currently connected to the gossip network.

tools.name: pcc_create_scope
tools.description: Create an execution scope for a job. Scopes define exactly which tool calls are allowed on a kernel during a job, with command budgets, retry limits, and time-to-live. Required before issuing SCOPED WRITE operations (protocol upload, run create, run action).

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to create the scope for

jobId.description: Job ID this scope is bound to (optional)

allowedTools.description: List of tool names allowed in this scope (e.g. ['ot2_protocol_upload', 'ot2_run_create', 'ot2_run_action'])

allowedSlots.description: Which deck slots may be accessed (e.g. [1, 2, 3, 9])

maxCommands.description: Maximum tool calls allowed in this scope (default 100)

protocolHash.description: SHA-256 hash of the approved protocol content. If set, protocol uploads are hash-verified.

tools.name: pcc_revoke_scope
tools.description: Revoke an execution scope immediately (emergency stop). All pending tool calls under this scope are rejected. The kernel enters a stopped state. A new scope must be created to resume.

tools.name: pcc_scope_audit
tools.description: Get the audit trail for an execution scope — every tool call made under this scope, with validation results, timestamps, and outcomes.

tools.name: pcc_relay_tool_call
tools.description: Relay a tool call to a device executor. The brain (LLM) posts tool calls here; the executor (on the device) polls for them and executes locally. Used for the brain/executor split architecture.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID of the target device

scopeId.description: Execution scope ID (required for SCOPED WRITE tools)

tools.name: pcc_get_tool_result
tools.description: Get the result of a previously relayed tool call. Poll this endpoint until the executor has processed the call and posted results.

callId.description: Tool call ID returned from pcc_relay_tool_call

tools.name: pcc_camera_latest
tools.description: Get the latest camera frame from a kernel as a JSON snapshot (base64 JPEG + metadata). For raw JPEG image, use GET /api/ot2/camera/latest directly.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to get camera frame from

tools.name: pcc_chat_send
tools.description: Send a chat message to a kernel's operator or agent. Used for human-in-the-loop communication during job execution, troubleshooting, and escalation.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to send the message to

tools.name: pcc_chat_history
tools.description: Get chat history with a kernel. Returns messages between agents, operators, and users for a specific kernel.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to get chat history for

tools.name: approve_registration
tools.description: Approve a submitted machine registration. Moves it from 'submitted' to 'approved' status, enabling the operator to activate and start accepting jobs.

tools.name: reject_registration
tools.description: Reject a machine registration with a reason. The operator can see the rejection reason and resubmit.

tools.name: activate_registration
tools.description: Activate an approved registration, making the operator's equipment live on the network and ready to accept jobs.

tools.name: prove_registration
tools.description: Fast-track: submit evidence that your device works and get auto-approved + activated immediately. No manual review needed. Submit a photo of test output, device health snapshot, or a full evidence bundle with completion events. If evidence meets requirements, registration jumps straight to 'active'.

evidence.description: Evidence proving the device works. Include at least one of: bundleHash+events, photoBase64, or deviceHealth.

bundleHash.description: SHA-256 hash of the evidence bundle

type.description: Event type: execution_completed, camera_snapshot, power_profile_summary, etc.

events.description: Evidence events from a test job

photoBase64.description: Base64-encoded photo of test output (printed page, machined part, etc.)

ipfsCid.description: IPFS CID if evidence was already uploaded

tools.name: list_registrations
tools.description: List all machine registrations on the network. See pending, approved, active, and rejected registrations. Public endpoint — no auth required.

tools.name: get_registration
tools.description: Get details of a specific machine registration by ID, including capabilities, pricing, operator info, and current status.

tools.name: near_status
tools.description: Get NEAR Protocol chain-abstraction integration status. Returns supported chains (near, eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon), supported assets (USDC, USDT, NEAR, ETH, WBTC), and capability flags. Use this to confirm cross-chain settlement is available before requesting quotes.

tools.name: near_quote
tools.description: Get a cross-chain payment quote from the NEAR 1Click solver network (chaindefuser.com). Provides optimal routing and fee estimates for funding PCC escrow contracts using any source asset on any supported chain. Call near_status first to confirm available chains/assets.

amount.description: Amount as an integer string in the smallest denomination (e.g. '1000000' for 1 USDC with 6 decimals)

recipient.description: Recipient address on the destination chain (optional)

tools.name: near_intent
tools.description: Submit a cross-chain payment intent to the NEAR 1Click solver network. Creates a signed intent that routes the payment atomically across chains. Call near_quote first to obtain a quoteId. Intents typically settle within 30-60 seconds — poll near_intent_status to track progress.

workflowId.description: PCC workflow or job ID this payment is for

recipient.description: Recipient address on the destination chain (optional)

tools.name: near_intent_status
tools.description: Check the settlement status of a submitted NEAR 1Click cross-chain payment intent. Statuses progress: pending → submitted → settled | failed. Returns txHash and explorerUrl when settled.

tools.name: protocol_state
tools.description: Read the PCCProtocol root contract state: current fee rate, total protocol fees collected, total escrow count, and registry addresses. Requires PCC_PROTOCOL_ADDRESS to be configured on the gateway.

tools.name: protocol_fee
tools.description: Calculate the protocol fee for a given USDC amount (6-decimal units). Returns the fee, the net amount after fee, and formatted versions of both. Use this before building escrow contracts to understand the true cost.

amount.description: Amount as a BigInt string in USDC 6-decimal units (e.g. '1000000000' = 1000 USDC)

tools.name: protocol_token_fees
tools.description: Get total protocol fees collected for a specific ERC-20 token address across all escrows. Returns raw wei amount and human-readable formatted value.

tools.name: protocol_escrow_fees
tools.description: Get protocol fees collected from a specific escrow contract. Also returns whether the escrow was deployed via the protocol factory. Useful for auditing fee flows.

tools.name: protocol_create_escrow
tools.description: Create a new MilestoneEscrow contract via the PCCProtocol factory on-chain. Protocol-deployed escrows have fee collection and registry tracking built in. Requires PCC_GATEWAY_PRIVATE_KEY write access.

cwmId.description: Capability Work Module ID as a 32-byte hex string (0x + 64 chars)

tools.name: pcc_dht_metrics
tools.description: Get a snapshot of DHT telemetry counters and recent events. Returns message counts, peer connection stats, query/announce rates, and a list of the last 50 metric events. Use for monitoring network health.

tools.name: marketplace_categories
tools.description: List all supplies and materials marketplace categories with the count of active listings in each. Categories cover the full spectrum of physical production inputs: raw metals, plastics, lab reagents, consumables, electronics, tooling, and more.

tools.name: marketplace_list_listings
tools.description: Search and filter supplies/materials marketplace listings. Operators buy raw materials here to fulfill capability contracts. Filter by category, in-stock status, location, or free-text query.

category.description: Filter by category: raw-metals, plastics-polymers, lab-reagents, lab-consumables, electronics, chemicals, biologicals, tooling, packaging, calibration, safety, other

query.description: Full-text search across name, description, and tags

tools.name: marketplace_get_listing
tools.description: Get full details of a specific supplies/materials marketplace listing by ID. Returns pricing, availability, lead time, location, and tags.

tools.name: marketplace_create_listing
tools.description: Create a new supplies/materials listing in the marketplace. Suppliers post available raw materials, lab reagents, tooling, or consumables for other operators to purchase.

category.description: Category: raw-metals, plastics-polymers, lab-reagents, lab-consumables, electronics, chemicals, biologicals, tooling, packaging, calibration, safety, other

unit.description: Unit of sale: kg, L, each, box, plate, etc.

inStock.description: Whether the item is currently available

leadTimeDays.description: Estimated lead time in business days

tools.name: marketplace_update_listing
tools.description: Update an existing supplies/materials listing (price, stock status, description, etc.). Pass only the fields you want to change.

pricePerUnit.description: New price per unit in USDC

tools.name: marketplace_delete_listing
tools.description: Remove a supplies/materials listing from the marketplace. The listing is immediately hidden from search results.

tools.name: marketplace_place_order
tools.description: Place a purchase order for supplies or materials. Calculates total price automatically (quantity × pricePerUnit). Returns an order with 'pending' status. Optionally links to an on-chain escrow for trustless settlement.

quantity.description: Quantity to order (must meet listing minOrder/maxOrder)

buyerId.description: Buyer entity ID (operator kernel ID, etc.)

escrowAddress.description: Optional on-chain escrow address for trustless settlement

tools.name: marketplace_list_orders
tools.description: List marketplace supply orders. Filter by buyerId, sellerId, or status. Returns order history with pricing and status.

buyerId.description: Filter to orders placed by this buyer

sellerId.description: Filter to orders received by this seller

tools.name: marketplace_get_order
tools.description: Get details of a specific supply order including the associated listing details, quantity, total price, status, and optional escrow address.

tools.name: system_telemetry
tools.description: Raw system state dump — actual DB rows for kernels, devices, jobs, evidence, registrations, capabilities, agent conversations, audit log. No fake numbers, no summaries.

tools.name: operator_poll_jobs
tools.description: Operator polls for pending jobs assigned to their kernel. Returns queued jobs ready for execution. Used by pcc-node daemon.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to poll jobs for

tools.name: operator_push_evidence
tools.description: Operator pushes evidence bundle from a completed job execution. Contains device ID, execution timestamp, result payload, and event timeline.

tools.name: operator_heartbeat
tools.description: Operator sends heartbeat with capability re-announcement. Keeps the kernel alive on the network and updates available capabilities.

tools.name: operator_update_job_status
tools.description: Operator updates job status during execution (running, completed, failed). Called by pcc-node as jobs progress.

tools.name: pcc_submit_paid_job
tools.description: Fast-track paid job: one call from DHT discovery to funded escrow + active scope. Auto-negotiates, quotes, creates escrow with milestones, creates execution scope. Returns jobId, scopeId, escrowId, quote with pricing adjustments, contract terms. For testnet, escrow is mock-funded automatically.

tools.name: pcc_job_complete
tools.description: Complete a job: gathers tool call audit trail from execution scopes, builds evidence bundle with SHA-256 hash, stores evidence, revokes scopes, and settles escrow (mock or real).

tools.name: pcc_job_settlement
tools.description: Get settlement status for a completed job: escrow address, evidence hash, milestones with amounts and status, paid amount, currency, and linked negotiation session.

tools.name: pcc_get_tool_manifest
tools.description: Get the tool manifest for a kernel's device type. Lists all available tools with their safety classification (read, safe_control, scoped_write, privileged) and input schemas. Use to understand what tools are available before making tool calls.

tools.name: pcc_relay_generic_tool_call
tools.description: Relay a tool call to any kernel's device executor via the generic relay (not OT-2 specific). Works with any device type. Safe tools (read/safe_control) don't need a scope. Scoped write tools require an active execution scope. Returns a call ID — poll pcc_get_tool_result for the response.

toolName.description: Tool name from the device manifest

scopeId.description: Execution scope ID (required for write operations)

tools.name: pcc_submit_request
tools.description: Submit a high-level capability request in natural language. The system automatically decomposes it into a capability DAG with dependencies, timelines, and budget allocation across fabrication, design, assembly, electronics, software, logistics, and verification nodes. Returns the request with full decomposed DAG. Example: 'Build a cute animatronic plush desk robot with servo-driven animations'.

description.description: Full natural language description of what needs to be built or done

urgency.description: Urgency level — affects cost multipliers (emergency: 2x cost, 0.5x time)

tools.name: pcc_list_requests
tools.description: List all capability requests with optional filtering. Shows status, decomposed DAG summary, estimated costs, and timelines.

tools.name: pcc_get_request
tools.description: Get a capability request by ID with the full decomposed DAG — all capability nodes, their dependencies, estimated costs/hours, assigned operators, and linked bounty IDs.

tools.name: pcc_decompose_request
tools.description: Re-trigger decomposition of an existing capability request. Overwrites the existing capability DAG with a fresh decomposition. Useful after updating the description or budget.

tools.name: pcc_publish_request
tools.description: Publish all pending capability nodes in a request as bounties. Each node becomes a bidding opportunity for operators. Returns the list of created bounty IDs linked to each capability node.

tools.name: pcc_get_request_dag
tools.description: Get the capability DAG (directed acyclic graph) for a request as adjacency data — nodes with all fields plus explicit edges showing dependency relationships. Useful for visualization or workflow planning.

tools.name: pcc_get_request_critical_path
tools.description: Get the critical path (longest dependency chain) for a capability request. The critical path determines the minimum calendar time to complete the request. Returns node IDs in order, the full node details, and total hours on the critical path.

tools.name: pcc_assign_node_operator
tools.description: Assign an operator to a specific capability node within a request. The node status changes to 'assigned'. Operators claim nodes to indicate they will execute that capability.

operatorId.description: Operator kernel ID or wallet address

tools.name: pcc_update_node_status
tools.description: Update the status of a capability node within a request. Valid transitions: pending → bidding → assigned → in_progress → completed (or failed). When all nodes complete, the request automatically moves to completed.

tools.name: pcc_update_request
tools.description: Update a capability request's title, description, budget, deadline, urgency, or contact info. Does not re-decompose — call pcc_decompose_request afterwards if you want a fresh DAG.

tools.name: pcc_cancel_request
tools.description: Cancel a capability request. Cancelled requests cannot be updated, decomposed, or published. This is a soft delete — the request remains visible with status 'cancelled'.

tools.name: pcc_generate_ui
tools.description: Generate a dynamic visual interface and serve it locally via pcc-node's UI server (localhost:3200). Supports built-in templates (plate-layout, protocol-builder, job-status, camera-viewer, device-config) or custom HTML. The UI appears in the operator's browser. Form submissions are queued for the agent to read via pcc_get_ui_submissions.

tools.name: pcc_oracle_status
tools.description: Check if the PCC verification oracle is online. Returns the oracle's EIP-712 signing address and chain ID. The oracle is required for all escrow settlements — no attestation means no fund release.

tools.name: pcc_oracle_verify
tools.description: Submit evidence for oracle verification. The oracle checks: evidence exists, hash matches, tier requirements met, no replay, operator identity valid. Returns a signed EIP-712 attestation that the escrow contract requires to release funds. This is the critical path — every settlement flows through this endpoint.

tools.name: pcc_protocol_fee
tools.description: Get the current protocol fee rate (2.35%, immutable) and fee recipient address. The fee is hardcoded in the PCCProtocol smart contract — no admin, no governance, no upgrade can change it.

tools.name: create_capability
tools.description: Register a capability instance for a kernel. Required before submitting jobs — the gateway needs at least one capability per kernel. Creates a liquid-handler, fdm, cnc-3axis, or other capability type.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID to register capability for

type.description: Capability type (e.g. liquid-handler, fdm, cnc-3axis, laser-cut, document-printing)

description.description: Description of what this capability does

tools.name: kernel_heartbeat
tools.description: Send a per-kernel heartbeat to keep the kernel marked online. Used by pcc-node daemons as an alternative to the operator relay heartbeat.

tools.name: kernel_announce_capabilities
tools.description: Announce capabilities for a kernel. Used by pcc-node daemons after hardware detection to register what the kernel can do.

devices.description: Device IDs that back these capabilities

tools.name: send_diagnostics
tools.description: Upload an encrypted diagnostic bundle when the operator's node has problems. The bundle is encrypted client-side with a retrieval code the operator must share with support before logs can be read. Use this when the operator reports errors, crashes, or misbehavior. The pcc-node CLI runs `pcc-node logs --send` locally to collect+encrypt; prefer that path when available. This tool is for agent-driven uploads when the bundle is already prepared.

kernelId.description: Kernel ID the diagnostics came from

bundleSize.description: Size of encrypted payload in bytes

logLineCount.description: How many log lines are in the bundle

collectedAt.description: ISO timestamp when bundle was collected

tools.name: send_support_message
tools.description: Send an operator support message to the PCC team. Creates a new support thread or appends to the operator's existing open thread. Can optionally attach a diagnostic retrieval code (from send_diagnostics) so support staff can decrypt logs. Discord webhook fires on every new message, so expect fast response. Use this whenever the operator says something is broken, confusing, or not behaving as expected.

message.description: The support message text — describe the problem concretely

subject.description: Optional thread subject (auto-generated from message if omitted)

retrievalCode.description: Optional diagnostic retrieval code to attach (from send_diagnostics)

systemInfo.description: Optional system context (platform, nodeVersion, daemonRunning, gatewayReachable)

tools.name: check_support_replies
tools.description: Check for admin replies on the operator's support threads. Call this periodically or when the operator asks 'did they respond yet?'. Returns all threads for this kernel and a hasUnreadReplies boolean indicating new admin messages.

tools.name: reply_to_support_thread
tools.description: Reply to an existing support thread. Use when the operator wants to add information to a thread started earlier. Needs the threadId from check_support_replies or the original send_support_message response.

retrievalCode.description: Optional diagnostic retrieval code to attach

tools.name: pcc_capture_challenge
tools.description: Issue a fresh block-anchored CaptureNonceChallenge for a job. The operator's device must render this nonce into the captured media (QR code, audio tone, etc.) before calling pcc_capture_upload. The nonce is derived from (challengeId, latest blockHash, workOutputRoot) so captures cannot be pre-computed. Returns challengeId, 64-char hex nonce, blockNumber, maxAgeSeconds (clamped to 120).

jobId.description: PCC job ID the capture belongs to

declaredClass.description: Capture class the operator plans to claim. Determines which gates the verifier will run.

requestedTtlSeconds.description: Requested challenge lifetime in seconds. Clamped to 120 server-side.

tools.name: pcc_capture_upload
tools.description: Upload a capture (photo / video / audio / sensor clip) with its CaptureManifest for G1..G6 verification. Bytes are base64-encoded inline; optional base64 C2PA manifest bytes can be supplied for CC3+ claims. The server runs the 6-gate CaptureVerifier and persists a PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL verdict. Returns {verdictId, verdict, verifiedClass, gatesPassed, gatesFailed, warnings, anchorCandidate, captureHash, manifestHash}.

manifest.description: CaptureManifest — ALCOA+-ready metadata: class, declaredAt (ISO-8601), deviceFingerprint, mediaHash (sha256:<hex>), optional challengeId. See CaptureManifestSchema in @pcc/spec.

captureBytesBase64.description: Base64-encoded capture bytes (image / video / audio / sensor clip). Hash must match manifest.mediaHash.

c2paManifestBase64.description: Optional base64-encoded C2PA manifest JUMBF bytes. Required when manifest.class >= CC3.

jobId.description: Job ID for telemetry binding. Falls back to manifest.jobId if omitted.

operatorId.description: Explicit operator ID. Falls back to the authenticated session userId.

challengeId.description: Challenge UUID to re-bind to the in-memory challenge cache (G3 freshness gate).

visualNonceEcho.description: The visual nonce value the operator rendered in-scene (QR payload, audio tone id, etc.).

submittedAt.description: Client-submitted timestamp (epoch ms). Used in drift detection.

tools.name: pcc_capture_anchor
tools.description: Anchor a PASS + anchor-candidate capture verdict to CaptureClassRegistry on-chain (Base Sepolia by default). Rejects FAIL/PARTIAL verdicts. Idempotent — re-submitting the same verdictId returns the existing anchor row. Returns 202 {status:'deferred'} if CaptureClassRegistry is not yet deployed (CAPTURE_REGISTRY_ADDRESS unset).

verdictId.description: The verdictId returned by pcc_capture_upload. Must be a PASS verdict with anchorCandidate=true.

tools.name: pcc_capture_status
tools.description: Fetch the combined verdict + on-chain anchor view for a single capture. Mirrors the verifier's DB shape plus the anchor tx metadata (txHash, blockNumber, gasUsed, explorerUrl). Anchor is null if the verdict was never anchored.

tools.name: pcc_list_verdicts
tools.description: List recent capture verdicts, newest first. Optionally filter by jobId. Default limit is 50, capped at 200 server-side. Returns {verdicts, count, limit, jobId}.

jobId.description: Filter by job ID. Omit for all verdicts across jobs.

tools.name: pcc_capture_class_registry
tools.description: Look up a capture's on-chain anchor record in CaptureClassRegistry by its 32-byte captureHash. Returns the registry address, captureHash, and decoded anchor tuple (declaredClass, verifiedClass, manifestHash, submittedBy, jobId, challengeId, blockAnchor, capturedAt, attestationsRoot, attesterCount). onchain is null if the capture was never anchored. Returns 202 deferred when CaptureClassRegistry is not yet deployed.

captureHash.description: Capture hash (32-byte). Accepts 0x-prefixed or unprefixed hex, or sha256:<hex> format. Padded server-side to bytes32.

tools.name: pcc_verifier_health
tools.description: Report CaptureVerifier health: which adapters are loaded (c2pa, webauthn, appattest, playintegrity), their staleness status, in-memory challenge cache size, whether CaptureClassRegistry is deployed, and the active PCC_NETWORK. Use this to diagnose why a capture class is being rejected or degraded.

tools.name: pcc_orchestrator_list_templates
tools.description: List the orchestrator templates the dashboard's chat console can drive. Each entry includes slug, display_name, description, produces_kind, capability_class (physical | digital), greeting, and api_base (the route prefix that serves the six session-driver routes for that template). Public — no auth required.

tools.name: pcc_orchestrator_match_capabilities
tools.description: Heuristic template matcher. Pass a free-text description of what you want to onboard (e.g. 'I run a CNC milling shop' or 'I have a Postgres database with a GraphQL endpoint') and the matcher returns all templates ranked by keyword score with a 'reason' string per match. Public — no auth required.

input.description: Free-text description of what you want to onboard.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_start
tools.description: Start a new physical-operator onboarding session. Returns a session_id used by every subsequent /api/onboard/* call. Auth-required.

url.description: Optional company website. If supplied, the orchestrator scrapes it on the next /scrape call.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_scrape
tools.description: Scrape a URL into the running physical-operator onboarding session. Triggers a stealth fetch + structured extraction (machines, hours, services, certifications). Returns a small JSON summary; full extraction is appended to the session's running profile and visible via /live-data. Auth-required.

url.description: URL to scrape (e.g. company About page).

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_ingest_docs
tools.description: Queue documents (datasheets, SOPs, MOPs, certifications) for ingestion into a physical-operator onboarding session. Document URLs may be local:// for files dropped in the chat console or full https:// URLs. Auth-required.

doc_urls.description: URLs of documents to ingest. Mix of local:// and https:// is fine.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_build_agent
tools.description: Finalise a physical-operator onboarding session: registers the operator on PCC, mints a wallet, writes the SEO mirror, returns the publication payload (capabilities, operator_id, discovery_url). Idempotent — safe to retry inside the same session_id. Auth-required.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_status
tools.description: Coarse status snapshot for a physical-operator onboarding session: current state, 0-100 progress, scraped_count, ingested_count, last_event, publication payload (if built). Cheap — designed for polling from the chat header. Auth-required.

tools.name: pcc_onboard_session_live_data
tools.description: Full event log for a physical-operator onboarding session — feeds the chat console's activity sidebar. Supports incremental polling via ?since=<unix-millis>. Returns the next cursor on every response. Auth-required.

since.description: Unix milliseconds cursor — returns only events with t > since. Use the 'cursor' field of the previous response for incremental polling.
